title: Cross-tenant observability prioritization slate
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working slate to prioritize which telemetry signals, traces, and dashboard surfaces we standardize across tenants for H1-Q2 observability work. The emphasis is fairness (no tenant blind spots), query-cost control, and a small set of operational primitives operators can use to investigate cross-tenant regressions quickly.

Why this is different: many previous docs focus on per-service dashboards or SLI composition. This canvas centers multi-tenant tradeoffs: signal cost allocation, tenant-weighted sampling, insight parity, and guardrails for cheap exploratory queries.

Goals (measurable):
- Produce a prioritized list of 12 signals to instrument across all tenant-facing inference routes by end of sprint (owner: Evan).
- Define trace/span naming + correlation fields and a tiered sampling policy that keeps trace volume under 5% growth while preserving high-fidelity for errors (owner: Priya).
- Prototype a tenant-tiling dashboard with 3 cross-tenant panels (latency heatmap, cost-per-1k-tokens, top root-cause spans) and a per-tenant drill-down link (owner: Maya).

Signal inventory (candidate items, short rationale):
- request.latency_ms (p50/p90/p99): core SLI for user-perceived latency; required for every route.
- token.emitted_count (per-request): economics baseline for cost allocation.
- kvcache.hits, kvcache.evictions: explains cold-cache tail latencies.
- model.variant.fallback_count: indicates graceful degradation behavior.
- output.hallucination_rate (manual eval flag / sampled): expensive but high-priority for quality SLOs; sampled annotation pipeline needed.
- trace.error_span_count: quick filter for error-heavy tenants.
- backend.queue_time_ms: isolates infra vs model compute.
- concurrency.by_tenant (running requests): helps detect noisy tenants.
- retry.count and throttle.count: operational signals for policy misconfiguration.
- prompt.length_tokens and prompt.template_id: correlate prompt characteristics with cost/latency.
- batch.size_distribution: informs batching optimization.
- embedding.kv_prefetch_miss: embedding-specific cold starts.

Metric definitions and units (short):
- request.latency_ms: milliseconds; measured server-side at ingress completion (not including network egress streaming time). Aggregation: histogram with explicit p quantiles.
- token.emitted_count: integer tokens emitted by model post-decoding; sum and per-1k normalization.
- kvcache.hits: count; ratio computed as hits / (hits+misses).

Trace/span conventions (proposal):
- Root span: span.name = "request". Attributes: tenant_id, route_id, request_id, session_id, model_id, model_variant.
- Model span: span.name = "model.invoke"; attributes: sequence_len, tokens_out, quantized_flag, kernel_path_hint.
- Cache span: span.name = "kvcache.lookup"; attributes: cache_key_hash, hit_bool.
- Use snake_case for attributes and hyphen-free span names. Keep attribute names stable so dashboards can query without remapping.

Sampling policy (tiered):
- Default sample rate: 0.5% of successful requests (baseline cheap sampling for health).
- Error amplification: all requests with status >=500 captured (100%).
- Latency amplification: top 2% latency tail per-route captured (100%). Implementation: sampling controller that accepts dynamic signals (route-config table) and annotation rules (error/latency override).
- Tenant-weighting: for tenants with fewer than X requests/day, raise sample rate to 2% to avoid blind spots. For top-5 noisy tenants, cap storage by dynamic downsampling.

Dashboard notes and layout (prototype):
- Top-level board: Cross-Tenant Health
  - Panel A: tenant latency heatmap (rows=tenant, cols=route); annotation overlays for rollout windows.
  - Panel B: normalized cost (USD per 1k tokens) by tenant; trendline and anomaly shading.
  - Panel C: Top 10 root-cause spans (ranked by error impact score) with tenant filter.
  - Quick actions: per-tenant link to timeline view (traces filtered by request_id) and runbook shortcuts.
- Drill-down: Tenant detail board (templated by tenant_id) with p50/p90/p99 latency, cache warmth, recent model variant rollouts, and manual quality sample set.

Alerting and SLO mapping:
- SLO candidate: 99th percentile latency per-route <= 600ms for hosted-api small models. Alerting on 10m burn rate > 10% for SLOs; page on tier 2 sustained violation + evidence in traces.
- Cost alert: sudden >30% day-over-day increase in token.emitted_count per-tenant should create a paging incident only if cost > $50/day change and correlated increase in request volume.

Operational runbooks/links (placeholders):
- Runbook: tenant-latency-investigation (link to Confluence page).
- Playbook snippet: when tenant p99 spikes, confirm model.variant, kvcache.evictions, and recent deploy tags. Attach trace sample of top 5 requests.

Data retention tiers & query-cost controls:
- Traces: 30d full fidelity for errors; 7d for amplified latency traces; 14d rollups for sampled traces (index-only).
- Metrics: high-cardinality metrics (prompt.template_id, tenant_id) stored as low-resolution aggregates after 90d.
- Query guards: dashboards must use templated time ranges and disallow open-ended across-all-tenants by default; exploratory queries require a cost budget tag.

Ownership and rollout plan (next 6 weeks):
- Week 1: finalize prioritized signals list and stable attribute names (this doc).
- Week 2-3: implement span naming and sampling controller; lightweight infra tests (Priya + Luis).
- Week 4: build dashboard wireframe and demo to SRE/SE teams (Maya).
- Week 5-6: pilot with 5 tenants, iterate sampling thresholds, finalize runbooks.

Open questions / risk notes:
- How do we surface output quality signals cheaply? Manual labeling pipeline cost is unknown and requires CS buy-in.
- Tenant-weighted sampling introduces complexity in billing/ingestion; need product discussion for chargeback visibility.
- Tradeoffs between trace fidelity and query-cost for big tenants; consider auto-expiry for non-error traces after review.

Action items (owners):
- Evan: draft finalized 12-signal list and stub PromQL/SQL queries (by 2026-02-19).
- Priya: prototype sampling controller logic + failure-mode tests (by 2026-02-26).
- Luis: storage/retention cost estimate and indexing plan (by 2026-03-01).
- Maya: dashboard wireframe + demo notes (by 2026-03-05).

Notes-to-self: keep the first iteration conservative—avoid adding high-cardinality labels until we have a clear use-case. Track query-cost impact as a first-class metric (telemetry.telemetry_query_cost_usd).

If you have immediate feedback, drop comments inline or ping #observability on Slack.
